'''Muthoot Finance Ltd''' is an Indian financial corporation and the largest gold loan [[Non-bank financial institution|NBFC]] in the country.<ref>{{cite news |title=Muthoot Finance cashback scheme launched for customers amid COVID-19 pandemic |url=https://www.zeebiz.com/companies/news-muthoot-finance-cashback-scheme-launched-for-customers-amid-covid-19-pandemic-131181 |work=Zee Business |date=14 July 2020}}</ref> In addition to financing gold loans, the company offers other forms of loans, insurance and [[Electronic funds transfer|money transfer]] services, and sells [[gold coins]]. The company is headquartered in [[Kochi]], [[Kerala]], and operates over 5,000 branches in the country. Outside India, Muthoot Finance is established in the UK, the US, and the [[United Arab Emirates]].

The company falls under the brand umbrella of the [[Muthoot Group]]. Its shares are listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange|BSE]] and [[National Stock Exchange of India|NSE]] since its [[initial public offering]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite news |title=Indian Billionaire George Muthoot's Pot of Gold |url=https://www.forbes.com/global/2011/1107/india-billionaires-11-george-muthoot-hoarders-kuttickat-rai.html |access-date=11 February 2023 |work=Forbes |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Muthoot Finance sets IPO price band at Rs 160-175 per share |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/muthoot-finance-sets-ipo-price-band-at-rs-160-175-per-share-18116-2011-04-13 |access-date=11 February 2023 |work=Business Today |date=13 April 2011 |language=en}}</ref> The target market of Muthoot Finance includes small businesses, vendors, farmers, traders, SME business owners, and salaried individuals.

The company was incorporated as a private limited company on 14 March 1997 with the name "The Muthoot Finance Private Limited" under the Companies Act.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/muthoot-finance-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-33218.cms|title=Muthoot Finance History|website=The Economic Times}}</ref>

On 18 November 2008, the company was converted into a public limited company with the name "Muthoot Finance Limited".<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/company-facts/muthootfinance/history/MF10?classic=true | title=Muthoot Finance Ltd. | publisher=Moneycontrol | accessdate=20 July 2020 }}</ref> During the year 2009–10, the company added 620 new branches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.business-standard.com/company/muthoot-finance-24769/information/company-history|title=Muthoot Finance Ltd.|work=Business Standard}}</ref>

In 2014, Muthoot Finance acquired a majority stake in Asia Asset Finance plc, a Sri Lankan publicly listed financial services company.<ref>{{cite news |title=Muthoot Finance acquires Sri Lankan company |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/muthoot-finance-acquires-sri-lankan-company/article6742204.ece |access-date=25 August 2023 |work=The Hindu |date=31 December 2014 |language=en-IN}}</ref>

In July 2016, Muthoot Finance acquired 46.83% of the capital of Belstar Investment and Finance Private Limited (BIFPL).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ndtv.com/business/muthoot-finance-ups-stake-in-belstar-investment-1437040|title=Muthoot Finance Ups Stake in Belstar Investment|website=NDTV.com|date=27 July 2016 }}</ref>

In May 2018, Muthoot Finance acquired Muthoot Money, a Non Deposit taking Non-Banking Financial Company.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/muthoot-finance-acquires-muthoot-money-118103000915_1.html|title=Muthoot Finance acquires Muthoot Money|website=Business Standard|date=30 October 2018 }}</ref>

==Philanthropy==
All of the philanthropic activities of Muthoot Finance are conducted through the Muthoot M George Foundation, which also conducts tree plantation drives<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.grow-trees.com/about/Testimonials.aspx
 |title=Grow Trees NGO Testimonials |publisher=Grow Trees}}</ref> and offers scholarships<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/muthoot-foundation-to-award-scholarships-110112400051_1.html |title=Muthoot Foundation to award scholarships |work=Business Standard|date=2010-11-24|accessdate=2014-01-25}}</ref> to the needy on a regular basis. The company is also involved in various philanthropic initiatives, which focus on education through M George Foundation,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/muthoot-foundation-to-award-scholarships-110112400051_1.html |title=Muthoot M George Foundation announced the launch of Muthoot M George Excellence Scholarships  |work=Business Standard|date=24 November 2010 }}</ref> environment, health, financial assistance and eco-friendliness.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.csridentity.com/india/muthootfinance.asp |title=Muthoot Finance CSR profile |publisher=CSR Identity}}</ref> With the assistance of the Credai Clean City Movement, the company is associated with the concept of an E-toilet, which was a public sanitation initiative.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-kerala/article2862334.ece |title=NATIONAL / KERALA : e-toilet opened in Children's Park |work=The Hindu|date=2012-02-05 |accessdate=2013-01-31}}</ref> Additionally, the company holds regular agricultural seminars by the name of "Ente Adukkalathottum" ("My Kitchen Garden") which educates farmers on the effects of pesticide residues in food and how to counter that for healthier living. It has also been actively involved in helping cancer patients, as well as individuals diagnosed with from kidney diseases, by financially covering medical expenses.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://santhimedicalinfo.org/Newsevents.aspx |title=NATIONAL / KERALA : Muthoot M George Foundation |publisher= NGO |accessdate=2014-01-25}}</ref>

The company runs the Kochi Chapter of the "Horn Not Ok Please" initiative, which raises awareness on the harmful effects of vehicular noise pollution.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/kochi/article352395.ece |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221194419/http://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/kochi/article352395.ece |url-status=dead |archive-date=21 February 2014 |title=NATIONAL / KERALA : Horn Not OK Please', a poster designing competition|work=The Hindu|date=2012-02-05 |accessdate=2013-01-31}}</ref> The company has also launched a Centre for Promoting/Creating Road Traffic Awareness at the office of the Asst. Commissioner of Police in Kochi to help raise awareness about road safety and the prevention of traffic accidents.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-kerala/article2542487.ece |title=Poster designing  |work=The Hindu|accessdate=2013-02-02}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kochivibe.com/in-kochi-horn-not-ok-please |title=In Kochi, Horn Not OK Please |publisher=kochivibe.com |accessdate=2013-02-02}}</ref>

In 2012, the Muthoot Group launched the first Paul George Memorial Tournament,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://zeenews.india.com/sports/cricket/sehwag-inaugurates-paul-george-memorial-tournament_770817.html |title=NATIONAL / DELHI: Sehwag inaugurates Paul George Memorial Tournament |publisher=Zee News |date=2013-10-14 |accessdate=2014-01-25}}</ref> which was aimed at Government School Children in the [[Delhi]] [[National Capital Region (India)|NCR]] region. The winners of the tournament were given scholarships.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/news/item/198103-t20-cricket-tournament-for-government-school-students |title=T20 cricket tournament for government school students|publisher=Sports.ndtv.com |date=2012-10-19 |accessdate=2013-01-31}}</ref>
